title: v3.0.0 claude upgrade writes a pre-commit chain block whose target no code in that build ever writes, so the installed gate enforces nothing and doctor never looks
body:
**`intent claude upgrade --apply` ON v3.0.0 REPORTS `written: .git/hooks/pre-commit` AND INSTALLS A GATE THAT ENFORCES NOTHING.** The hook it writes is a seven-line chain block that execs `.git/hooks/pre-commit.intent` if that file is executable. **No code in v3.0.0 ever writes that file, and no template for it ships in that build.** The `[ -x ... ]` test is false forever, the hook exits 0, and every commit passes ungated.

## Driven on v3.0.0 (`80d8b2ca`), from a faithful install tree

The binary was placed at `<install>/bin/intent` with `git archive v3.0.0 lib/templates` unpacked alongside it, because `claude upgrade` refuses when it cannot locate its own install. Fresh `git init` + `intent init` + `intent claude upgrade --apply`:

```
written: .git/hooks/pre-commit
$ ls .git/hooks | grep -v sample
pre-commit
$ [ -e .git/hooks/pre-commit.intent ] && echo PRESENT || echo ABSENT
ABSENT
```

The installed carrier, in full:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

# intent-chain-block:start (generated by intent claude upgrade)
_intent_chain="$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks 2>/dev/null)/pre-commit.intent"
if [ -x "$_intent_chain" ]; then
  "$_intent_chain" "$@" || exit $?
fi
# intent-chain-block:end
```

**Six candidate writers were driven, none writes the chained file:** `claude upgrade --apply`, `claude upgrade --apply --force`, `upgrade`, `claude skills sync`, `lang init shell`, `doctor`. After each, `.git/hooks/` holds `pre-commit` and nothing else.

## The controls, because a silent hook and an absent hook look identical

**CONTROL 1 -- the listing can see the file arrive.** `touch .git/hooks/pre-commit.intent` and the same listing immediately reports `pre-commit pre-commit.intent`. So the six negatives above are real negatives and not a blind instrument.

**CONTROL 2 -- the gate is not merely quiet; nothing runs it.** Copy the shipped gate body into place by hand and commit:

```
$ cp lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit.sh .git/hooks/pre-commit.intent && chmod +x
$ git commit -m armC
guards: 1 ran, 3 skipped (not applicable)
```

**The gate speaks the moment it is reachable.** In the shipped state it prints nothing because it is never executed.

**CONTROL 3 -- `doctor` is not silent in general.** On the same project `intent doctor` emits three findings (`backup-stale`, two `view-skew`) and mentions the gate, the hook, or `pre-commit` **zero** times. So the absence of a gate finding is the check declining to look, not a healthy project.

## Where the writer went

`install_carrier` -- the function that writes `lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit-shim.sh` to `<hooks>/pre-commit.intent`, cited by `0105` and `0108` -- **does not exist at the cut.** `git grep 'install_carrier' v3.0.0 -- native/rust` returns nothing; at `HEAD` it is `canon.rs:492`. `lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit-shim.sh` is likewise absent from the v3.0.0 tree. **The carrier installer landed after the tag; the chain block that depends on it shipped in the tag.**

## NOT a duplicate of the shim family, and the difference is the direction

`0105`, `0107`, `0108` and `0113` all describe a **working shim carrier reported as broken** -- `doctor` reads the carrier, expects the gate body's marker, and reds an estate whose guards demonstrably run. Every one of them is about the shim era, which begins after this cut.

**This is the reflection: no carrier at all, and nothing reports it.** A false red announces itself and gets diagnosed -- 0108 records three nodes doing exactly that. A gate that was never installed is indistinguishable, from every surface the tool offers, from a gate that passed. It is the state `0108`'s own message names and fears -- *every surface reports health while nothing is enforced* -- reached on the published build by the opposite route.

## Blast radius

**Every consumer who installs the gate on v3.0.0 through the documented verb.** `languages` is `[]` at `intent init`, so `0242`'s silent-scope defect sits behind this one and cannot even be reached: the scope report never runs because the file holding it is never invoked.

The estates that hoisted to a source build after the tag have the carrier and are unaffected; this is a property of the published artefact.

## What would settle it

Either the version that emits the chain block also installs the carrier it names, or `claude upgrade` refuses to write a chain block whose target it cannot provide. **A carrier that chains to nothing should not report `written:`.** `doctor`'s gate check should also answer for the absent-carrier case, which on this build it does not reach at all.

Found while dispositioning `0242` for AC-02.3 against the published build.
